items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: File paths embedded in pull requests can inject CI workflow commands through command-line error messages
items.summary: Impact0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. The fix escapes the command openers in compose-lint's own output, but not in the argument parser's error messages. When a repository path reaches compose-lint's arguments without a -- before it, the argument parser prints it raw in its error message. That includes a carriage return, which the runner treats as a line break, so a command can also start a new line there.A pull request can therefore create annotations, fold or hide parts of the job log, or issue other commands the runner accepts, when CI runs compose-lint over it, before anyone reviews it. The pass/fail result is not changed.Affected setups pass repository paths to compose-lint without a -- before them: the pre-commit hook when args: is set without the documented trailing --, or the compose-lint package or Docker image called that way in a workflow. The pre-commit hook's default configuration passes -- and is not affected. The GitHub Action turns command processing off around each compose-lint run, so it is not affected.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review. It was first published as part of GHSA-r7j4-crjv-h467, together with four other gaps in the same fix. Each gap now has its own advisory.Docker image. composelint/compose-lint tag 0.31.0 and the matching minor tag are affected, as was latest while it pointed to 0.31.0.Releases before 0.31.0 are covered by GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6.PatchesFixed in 0.32.0. The argument parser's messages go through the same sanitizer as the rest of compose-lint's output.WorkaroundsUpgrade to 0.32.0 or later.End the pre-commit hook's args: with --, and put -- before file paths when calling compose-lint directly.On GitHub Actions, use the tmatens/compose-lint Action, or bracket the compose-lint step with ::stop-commands::<random token> and ::<token>::, as the Action does.ReproductionOn compose-lint 0.31.0 on a GitHub-hosted runner (runner 2.337.0), compose-lint '--##[warning]X/compose.yml' with no -- creates an annotation. The same path after -- creates none. The composelint/compose-lint:0.31.0 image produces byte-identical output to the package.Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-8v59-qmwv-4p6qhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-125123https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/945https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/542e63126f795564a65c63887ea0dc558a500688https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.32.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8v59-qmwv-4p6q

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: Text in a pull request can issue CI workflow commands through JSON and SARIF output on stdout
items.summary: Impact0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. --format json and --format sarif output never passed through that fix, so ##[ inside a service name or other value reaches the log intact when the output is printed to stdout rather than written to a file. The runner acts on ##[ in the middle of a line, so the JSON layout does not prevent it.A pull request can therefore create annotations, fold or hide parts of the job log, or issue other commands the runner accepts, when CI runs compose-lint over it, before anyone reviews it. The pass/fail result is not changed.Affected setups print JSON or SARIF output to a CI log from the compose-lint package, the pre-commit hook or the Docker image. Writing that output to a file, which SARIF upload requires, is not affected. The GitHub Action turns command processing off around each compose-lint run, so it is not affected.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review. It was first published as part of GHSA-r7j4-crjv-h467, together with four other gaps in the same fix. Each gap now has its own advisory.Docker image. composelint/compose-lint tag 0.31.0 and the matching minor tag are affected, as was latest while it pointed to 0.31.0.Releases before 0.31.0 are covered by GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6.PatchesFixed in 0.32.0. JSON and SARIF on stdout escape ##[ inside strings as \u005b, which decodes to the same data.WorkaroundsUpgrade to 0.32.0 or later.Write --format json and --format sarif output to a file rather than the log.On GitHub Actions, use the tmatens/compose-lint Action, or bracket the compose-lint step with ::stop-commands::<random token> and ::<token>::, as the Action does.ReproductionOn compose-lint 0.31.0 on a GitHub-hosted runner (runner 2.337.0), a service named a##[warning]X, linted with --format json or --format sarif to stdout, creates annotations. The same file linted with the text report creates none. The composelint/compose-lint:0.31.0 image produces byte-identical output to the package.Referenceshttps://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/security/advisories/GHSA-hr4h-4c45-v4q4https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-125122https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/pull/945https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/commit/542e63126f795564a65c63887ea0dc558a500688https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/releases/tag/v0.32.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hr4h-4c45-v4q4

items.title: [compose-lint] compose-lint: Text in a pull request can still issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's output
items.summary: Impact0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. The fix escapes the command openers in everything compose-lint prints, and the 0.31.0 changelog says the report "escapes both openers (also covering Azure Pipelines)". Five paths were left open:Unicode whitespace before a line-leading ::. The runner strips all Unicode whitespace from the start of a line before it looks for a command. compose-lint only accounted for spaces and tabs, so a no-break space or another Unicode space ahead of :: is not escaped. It can come from a Compose value, or from a file name: the text report's file heading and per-file summary, and the fix summary on stderr, start with the path as given, so a directory named with a leading no-break space followed by :: puts a command at the start of a line. This reaches those lines, the text report's fix guidance, the fix dry-run diff, and continuation lines of stderr diagnostics.JSON and SARIF printed to stdout. --format json and --format sarif output never passed through the sanitizer, so ##[ inside a service name or other value reaches the log intact when the output isn't redirected to a file.Command-line errors. When a repository path reaches compose-lint's arguments without a -- before it, the argument parser prints it raw in its error message. That includes a carriage return, which the runner treats as a line break, so a command can also start a new line there.Azure Pipelines. ##vso[ logging commands were not escaped on any path, despite the changelog's Azure claim.An error message in the GitHub Action (0.30.0 and 0.31.0). When sarif-file: names a file in a subdirectory that can't be created, the Action prints the directory's resolved path in an error message, outside the window in which it turns command processing off. A pull request can commit a symlink on that path to a directory whose name contains a newline followed by a command. The documented setup, sarif-file: results.sarif at the repository root, is not affected.A pull request can therefore create annotations, fold or hide parts of the job log, or issue other commands the runner accepts, when CI runs compose-lint over it, before anyone reviews it. The pass/fail result is not changed.Affected setups are those that print compose-lint's output to a CI log without the GitHub Action: the compose-lint package run directly in a workflow, the pre-commit hook run in CI, and the Docker image. The pre-commit hook is affected in its default configuration: it passes each changed file's path to compose-lint, and a path whose directory name starts with Unicode whitespace and :: reaches the report's file heading. The JSON/SARIF and command-line paths also need output left on stdout, or args: without the documented trailing --, which is why they alone would score lower. The GitHub Action turns command processing off around each compose-lint run, so of these paths only its own error message affects it, and only when sarif-file: points into a subdirectory. That setup is outside the documented one, which is why that path alone would also score lower.Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.Docker image. composelint/compose-lint tag 0.31.0, the matching minor tag, and latest are affected.Releases before 0.31.0 are covered by GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, except the Action's error message, which also affects Action 0.30.0.PatchesFixed in 0.32.0. The line-start escaping covers every character the runner strips before ::, so it holds for quoted values and file names alike. JSON and SARIF on stdout escape ##[ inside strings as \u005b, which decodes to the same data. argparse's own messages go through the same sanitizer. ##vso[ is escaped everywhere. In the Action, the SARIF-directory error names the sarif-file: input as written.WorkaroundsUpgrade to 0.32.0 or later.On GitHub Actions, use the tmatens/compose-lint Action, or bracket the compose-lint step with ::stop-commands::<random token> and ::<token>::, as the Action does.In the Action, keep sarif-file at the workspace root, for example sarif-file: results.sarif.Write --format json and --format sarif output to a file rather than the log.End the pre-commit hook's args: with --. This closes the command-line path only; it does not stop a file name at the start of a report line, so in CI also bracket the pre-commit step with ::stop-commands:: as above.On Azure Pipelines, don't print compose-lint's output from runs over untrusted pull requests to the job log.ReproductionOn compose-lint 0.31.0 on a GitHub-hosted runner (runner 2.337.0), each of the following creates an annotation:a Compose file with image: "nginx\n\u00a0::notice::X", linted with the text report;a directory named \u00a0::notice::X (a no-break space, then ::notice::X) holding a compose.yml, linted with compose-lint -- '<that directory>/compose.yml', or by the pre-commit hook in its default configuration;a service named a##[warning]X, linted with --format jso
